name: Queets River
blurb: The Olympic Peninsula's wildest rain-forest river — gravel bars, elk and very few people.

sections.notes: NPS describes Class II–III water, year-round log-jam hazards and late-summer low water/debris. Check current conditions before launching. Park entrance fees apply when required; follow posted access and road restrictions.
sections.distanceReview: The 6.8-mile planning value came with the older Queets Trailhead label. This map now uses the separately documented Queets Campground boat launch. The old hydrography traces about 6.42 miles but follows abandoned channels in places; neither that trace nor the old planning value is a verified distance for the corrected endpoint.

notices.title: Put-in corrected to Queets Campground
notices.text: This trip now starts at the NPS-documented campground boat launch. The older “Queets Trailhead” label referred to a different nearby location. The map shows the launch area; confirm the usable gravel-bar entry on site. The listed planning mileage remains under review.
notices.sourceName: National Park Service — Queets area brochure

notices.title: Queets: changing channels, wood and rough roads
notices.text: Expect log jams and shifting gravel bars; scout ahead. The upper approach uses narrow forest roads unsuitable for trailers or large RVs. Winter storms can damage roads and launches. Check the NPS roads page before your shuttle.
notices.sourceName: National Park Service — Queets access and road guidance

sections.routeReview: A dotted course is withheld: the available older river geometry follows vegetated or abandoned channels in places. These access-area markers do not identify a runnable channel or an exact carry to the water.
